_meta.description: Illustrative carbon-contribution options, described by project TYPE and certification standard rather than by vendor. No real provider is named, priced or endorsed here.
_meta.integrity_warning: Offsetting does not cancel a journey's emissions. Independent investigations of forestry-based credits have found substantial over-crediting, and permanence, additionality and leakage remain unresolved for most project types. The mitigation hierarchy applies: avoid the journey, then shift to a lower-carbon mode, then reduce what remains, and only then contribute to a climate project for the residual. This assistant therefore presents contributions AFTER reduction options, never instead of them.
_meta.price_basis: Indicative 2026 voluntary-market ranges in EUR per tonne CO2e. Real prices vary widely by vintage, registry and volume.
_meta.standards_are_real: Gold Standard, Verra VCS, Puro.earth and the EU CRCF are real certification frameworks. Their appearance here describes the project category only.

providers.caveat: Avoided-emission credits depend on a counterfactual baseline that cannot be observed directly; usage rates are often lower than assumed.
Forestry credits carry the weakest evidence base of the categories listed here. Sequestration is reversible and frequently over-estimated.
Durable and measurable, but roughly six times the price of avoidance credits; supply is limited.
Highly durable, but measurement of actual uptake in field conditions is still maturing.

providers.type: Direct air capture with geological storage
providers.caveat: The most rigorous option and the most expensive; capacity is a tiny fraction of voluntary-market demand.

reduction_first_prompts: Shifting one return short-haul flight to rail typically saves more CO2e than a year of average household recycling.
Adding one night to the stay and taking a slower overland route usually cuts journey emissions by more than any contribution you could buy for the same money.
Choosing accommodation within walking distance of a station removes the airport-transfer leg entirely, which is often 5-10% of a short trip's footprint.
